It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. div.head: ECf 11.1 A 5
div.ab: Tales enim metas et fines, ut predicte sunt, constituit et imposuit corone regni huius dominus Eleutherius papa sententia sua — anno scilicet CXXXVII post passionem Christi —, qui primo destinauit coronam benedictam Britannie et Christianitatem, Deo inspirante, Lucio regi Britonum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 635 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 11, 1, and numbers 11, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 11, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

Bryt. stets Ld; Bretorum K Co
Bryt. always Ld; Bretorum K Co

div.ab: For such bounds and borders, as have been said above, the lord Pope Eleutherius established and imposed on the crown of this kingdom by his sentence — namely in the 137th year after the Passion of Christ —, who first, by God's inspiration, sent the blessed crown of Britain and Christianity to Lucius, king of the Britons.

note.seg: Vgl. ebd. Lucius; als Urquelle betrachtet den Liber Pontificalis Rom. Mommsen Chron. min. III (Mon. Germ., Auct. antiquiss. 13, 1898) p. 115. Ganz andere [m. E. nicht zutreffende] Erklärung versucht Alf. Anscombe in Miscell. pres. to Kuno Meyer (Halle 1912): der gemeinte Papst sei Liberius, Lucius vicarius Britanniarum in London, das Jahr 363/4. — LXVII14 Rs

Cf. ibid. Lucius; Mommsen, Chron. min. III (Mon. Germ., Auct. antiquiss. 13, 1898) p. 115, regards the Liber Pontificalis Rom. as the original source. Alf. Anscombe in Miscell. pres. to Kuno Meyer (Halle 1912) attempts an entirely different [in my opinion incorrect] explanation: the pope meant is Liberius, Lucius the vicarius Britanniarum in London, the year 363/4. — LXVII14 Rs
